title: Gasoline Shortages Trigger Long Queues, Station Closures Across Tehran as Sanctions Squeeze Tightens
detail: Long queues formed at petrol stations across Tehran, with several stations closing or experiencing disruptions in eastern, southern, central, and northern districts; similar shortages were reported in Kerman and Mashhad. Fereydoun Yassami, Tehran regional manager of the National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company, said more than 26 million litres of gasoline were distributed in the capital on Monday — a record for the current Iranian year, roughly 30% above usual demand — driven by panic buying. Iran faces a structural petrol deficit of roughly 15 million litres a day against total demand of about 135 million litres, a gap widened by the US naval blockade (in effect since July 14), war-damaged refining and storage/distribution infrastructure, and constrained northern import routes affected by the Ukraine war. Mohsen Haji Mirzai, head of President Pezeshkian's office, said a cut to petrol quotas (currently 20 litres) was 'certain' and that non-subsidized fuel prices would rise, though subsidized prices would hold; a pilot price increase in Kerman province was reversed within hours after public backlash. Pezeshkian himself asked rhetorically, 'Who said the government should buy petrol at 1.3 million rials per litre and then sell it for 15,000 rials?' Energy analyst Morteza Behrouzifar warned that raising prices now 'could have undesirable social and economic consequences' given how much pressure the public is already under. The National Iranian Oil Products Distribution Company maintained the supply chain remains stable and blamed the lines on rumor-driven panic buying and delivery delays.

title: Tanker AL SALAM II Struck Above Waterline by Unknown Projectile Near Khasab, Strait of Hormuz
detail: UKMTO issued Advisory 121-26 (reported publicly Aug 27) confirming that the tanker AL SALAM II was struck just above the waterline by an unknown projectile at 17:30 UTC on Aug 25 while transiting near Khasab, Oman, at the Strait of Hormuz's Musandam entrance — the second unclaimed projectile strike on a tanker in the strait within two days, after the Metro Venetian incident near Ash Shishah on Aug 24. The impact opened a small hole and caused a fire, which the crew extinguished; all crew members were reported safe with no environmental impact. The vessel later anchored roughly 0.8 nautical miles northwest of Jazirat Tawakkul and required tug assistance. No government or armed group has claimed responsibility.

confidenceReason: Confirmed by UKMTO advisory and multiple outlets, but the projectile's origin is unattributed and no actor has claimed the strike.
